subject: Math
prompt: A sample of a certain isotope takes $18$ years to decay to half its original mass. The function $m(t) = 320(0.5)^\frac{t}{(18)}$ gives the approximate mass of this isotope, in grams, that remains $t$ years after a $320$-gram sample starts to decay. Which statement is the best interpretation of $m(72) = 20$ in this context?

choices.A: Approximately $20$ grams of the sample remains $72$ years after the sample starts to decay.
choices.B: The mass of the sample has decreased by approximately $20$ grams $72$ years after the sample starts to decay.
choices.C: The mass of the sample has decreased by approximately $72$ grams $20$ years after the sample starts to decay.
choices.D: Approximately $72$ grams of the sample remains $20$ years after the sample starts to decay.

explanation:
Choice A is correct. In the given function, $m(t)$ represents the approximate mass, in grams, of the sample that remains $t$ years after the sample starts to decay. It follows that the best interpretation of $m(72) = 20$ is that approximately $20$ grams of the sample remains $72$ years after the sample starts to decay.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. The mass of the sample has decreased by approximately $320 - 20$, or $300$, grams, not $20$ grams, $72$ years after the sample starts to decay.
